## Problem
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py` is now fail-CLOSED for `os.environ` accesses (bug
`blocky-matricidal-squid`, Gerrit 1979): an attribute it cannot classify aborts the
generator naming the site. The OTHER half of the same blind spot is untouched and still
fails OPEN.

`KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` maps a project env-read helper name to the argument position holding
the env-var name. A helper ABSENT from that table is not an error -- it is invisible. The
scan walks past every call to it, the drift gate stays green, and the variables it reads
are simply missing from `docs/env-vars.md`.

This is not speculative. It has already cost documentation once: bug
`b00f-c62e-d3b9-4e63` (scared-restored-swallow) lost FOUR undocumented vars to a missing
`_llm_float` row, and the fix added the row while explicitly recording that the CLASS
stayed open. The comment sits in the file today:

    Omitting this one cost four undocumented vars (bug b00f): a helper absent from this
    table is not an error, it is INVISIBLE -- the scan walks past every call and the drift
    gate stays green, so a clean `--check` proves agreement with the generator, never
    completeness.

So the generator now has two different failure postures for the same underlying hazard:
an unknown `os.environ` accessor stops the build, while an unknown helper is silent.

## Why it is harder than the os.environ half
`os.environ` is a single named object, so "every attribute access on it" is a closed set an
AST pass can enumerate and classify. A helper is an arbitrary local function; there is no
syntactic marker that says "this one reads the environment". Any fix has to invent that
signal. Sketches, to be decided on evidence rather than picked from this list:
- an explicit decorator or naming convention on env-read helpers that the scan can key on
- flagging any function whose body contains a recognised env read but whose name is not in
  `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` -- a one-level dataflow check, catching the "wrote a new shim and
  forgot the row" case that has actually happened
- accepting fail-open here and instead asserting COVERAGE some other way

Note the second option would have caught b00f exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A new env-read helper added to `src/rebar` WITHOUT a `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` row produces
      a build failure naming the site — using a helper shape that escapes the EXISTING guard in
      `tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py`, verified RED before the fix exists,
      a loud failure, proven by a test that adds such a helper and asserts the failure --
      and that FAILS against today's generator.
- [x] The `_llm_float`/b00f scenario is replayed as a regression test: removing a row for a
      helper that IS used must not silently shrink the registry.
- [x] No false positives on the current tree: `make lint` and the full suite stay green,
      and `docs/env-vars.md` gains ONLY genuine env reads. Measured on the landed commit:
      162 -> 164, the delta being exactly `REBAR_GATE_REF` and `REBAR_GATE_SOURCE` (plus
      `config.py` joining `JIRA_API_TOKEN`'s provenance). The original "(162 keys)" wording
      assumed the gap was LATENT, as in sibling 1979; this ticket's own RCA measured it LIVE,
      so holding the doc at 162 would mean shipping a generator that still drops two real
      operator-settable vars. Corrected after the fact and recorded in the close comment --
      the substance (no SPURIOUS keys) is what was met.
- [x] If fail-closed is judged infeasible for helpers, record WHY on this ticket and name
      the compensating signal instead -- silence is not an acceptable close. VACUOUS: the
      escape clause never triggered, because fail-closed WAS achieved via the
      parameterized-shim predicate. The design decision and the two rejected alternatives are
      in the RCA comment, section 6.

## Provenance
Recorded 2026-08-20 while fixing `blocky-matricidal-squid`. Deliberately NOT folded into
that change: widening the os.environ recogniser is a closed, enumerable problem, and this
one needs a design decision. Filed rather than left implied-fixed by the sibling's
fail-closed language.

## Existing coverage (acknowledged)

`tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py` already carries a durable guard over
`KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`. A naively-written new test can therefore pass against today's tree without
exercising the fail-open gap this ticket is about, so a green result from such a test proves
nothing.

Any test written for AC #1 must use a helper shape that escapes **both** the existing guard in
that module **and** whatever new detection this ticket adds — otherwise it is measuring the old
guard, not the new one. Demonstrate that by seeding the shape and observing RED before the fix
exists, per the RED-first requirement below.

Note also that `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` imports `scan` and `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS` and
transitively scans the real tree across roughly 40 held-out tests. That is a repo-wide oracle the
fast gates do not run, and it bit the sibling change (1979) twice — budget for it.
